SA Drone technology inventions

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
There is fierce competition in the ever expanding world of Drones. Two South African inventions have grabbed international support for their inventions,one assisting farmers and the other to clean up the water ways.


Summary:
Capetonian inventor Richard Hardiman’s watched men in a boat scooping up waste that had been blown into the water with a pool scoop at the Waterfront in cape Town- an exercise in futility, no sooner had they scooped it up more blew in. To his surprise this method of was used in most harbours around the world. This was the inspiration for Wasteshark –using drone technology this autonomous floating device swallows up litter moving into places that people can’t. It can operate 16 hours a day sucking up 350 kg of trash. Richard’s invention was picked up by the Port of Rotterdam as part of an accelerator program for innovations in the management of harbours; suddenly an idea developed in his pool in Cape Town had international attention. Tested in Cape Town during the Volvo yacht race the Waterfront is now using two of the devices. But Wasteshark can do far more than collect trash, it also collects data on the quality of the water and scoops up invasive weeds and algae blooms.
The 2nd drone application is called Aeroview- this uses the conventional aerial drone. Aeroview is a software program which uses a combination of satellite and drone images to map farm lands. The images are then converted into a software program that gives farmers detailed information of every tree on their farm. They monitor tree health noting changes over time. GPS co-ordinates of a specific trees are sent to the farm manager enabling the farmer to pin point the exact treatment required. Nedbank are using Aeroview on 200 of the farms that require Agri- Finance. Accurate yields can now be predicted by monitoring the canopy size and tree health. Accurate insurance cover is now possible giving banks more security on issuing finance to farmers.
Aeroview was selected by Google Launch Pad as one of the most promising products in the emerging market

Press Release:


SA Drone Technology
There’s fierce competition in the ever-expanding world of high-tech drones, but two South African inventions have grabbed international attention. From cleaning our waterways to clever solutions for farming, these drones are no longer just big, expensive toys for digital enthusiasts. Carte Blanche explores how locally developed technology is helping to improve lives.


Script:


Drones are the future- they have moved far beyond remote warfare or capturing stunning aerial footage, they will deliver pizza, medicine, track game and even criminals, operating in the air and in water. In 10 years’ time it’s estimated that it will be a 90 billion dollar industry, and two South Africa start-up companies are ensuring they have a piece of the action. Richard Hardiman’s aqua drone gobbles up waste
Richard 08 32 40 21 Essentially it's a floating waste paper basket, I don't really make it any more of it than that. The technology and software behind it is far greater than a waste paper basket but it is a essential job is to go out and collect floating trash out of water before it sinks on the bottom or gets out of the harbour wall
Script And James Paterson is improving productivity on farms
James The farmer spends all year trying to produce a crop and then something can go wrong along …so we're really trying to mitigate those risks throughout the season to ensure that at the end he's got a successful crop
Script: Growing up on a farm in Citrusdal James sees this as the future of farming, and Richard hopes to make a dent in Plastic in the ocean which is killing marine life.
Link: Trying to keep waterways and harbours free from waste is an on-going challenge for port authorities and sadly most of it gets swept out to sea
Script: Port Manager Mpumi Dweba- Kwetana says the winter storms are the worst time of year
Dweba “Last year we had a storm in the port of Cape Town and we collected about 33 tons of waste
Script: Richard was sure he could design a drone to tackle the problem.
Richard “I was watching two guys in a boat I don't even think it was as fancy a boat as the one they have now I think it was a rubber duck they were taking the trash out with that and it was particularly windy day …and trash was slowly going up to the harbour wall. It wasn’t so much the waste going in the water but the inefficiency of the process
Script: It may look really small but it can buzz about for 16 hours a day in between the massive vessels, collecting 500 kg of waste, depending on the size of the basket.
Richard Somewhere the size of Cape Town harbour you would need 4 or 5 of those on a daily basis
Script: His concept was so ingenious that a Rotterdam company looking for innovations in the maritime space selected it from a 1000 other entries
Richard “We got through to the top 10 accelerator which was fantastic and then I had to move there for 3 months
Script: He has spent the last 3 years developing Wasteshark in Rotterdam
Richard ‘’I took an idea that I wanted to start here and make African and took it overseas and they paid to developed it and now we are back here as a commercial unit
Script: Aerobotics has also received international endorsement; selected by Google launch pad along with 24 other countries, they attended an accelerator workshop in San Francisco
James “we also realized that we can compete with these companies around the world. 07 33 11 13 We're actually doing something quite unique especially in the tree crops space
Script: Aeroview uses a combination of drone and satellite imagery, creating detailed images of every plant, it can even distinguish the crops from the weeds. The program has a classification system that displays changes in crop health, moving from red, which is stressed, to green creating a tool for early problem detection.
James The drones we are using now they fly up quite high between 80 and 100 metres above the ground but you are still getting two to three centimetre resolution in the picture. So if you zoom in you can see leaves on the tree and we use this data to reconstruct the whole tree and the whole orchard in three dimensions. And that's the data we use to extract our per tree health matrix our heights and our volumes.
Script: Hein Gerber is a citrus farmer and consultant to farms across the country. He has been testing Aeroview on this 6 hectare lemon farm for the last 5 years
LinksWhen Hein took over this orchard in 2013 it was in a very poor state but using Aeroview he has managed to radically transform it
Hein 06 27 00 00 “We went from sort of 30 tons a hectare to 72 to just …over 100.
Script: When you are in the middle of an orchard it’s difficult to see what the problems are with the naked eye, but this gives the birdseye view so farmers can pin point problem areas and micro manage them.
Hein 06 29 54 03 So despite after year one the orchard looking really nice from the outside from the inside ..the trees was experiencing stress. …this orchard had almost a circle in the middle that was always showing up red. …And then when we investigated we saw well it's just the soil texture difference it's a very sandy spot.
Script. They applied 6 tons of manure to that specific patch, instead of the whole orchard and within two weeks it turned green on the map.
Hein 06 35 41 06 So it's a lot more efficient. It's simple. It's really effective …. then another one is assisting with this water crisis that we're experiencing in the Western Cape and there specifically we looking at you know what's the ideal schedule with the minimum amount of water. So what's the minimum amount of water that you can give but still get a marketable fruit size.
Script: Wasteshark also gathers data like chemical and bacterial content
Richard 08 35 42 14 So we literally put probes into the water and it quantifies anything you want we have space for 256 probes that we can put on an collect data points
Link 08 46 15 12 Wasteshark was first used here at the V&A Waterfront during the Volvo yacht race at the end of last year and currently it’s under trial to see how effective it is in keeping these waterways free from waste
Donald Kau we are the host port for the Volvo Ocean Race and one of the key messages in the campaign with the Volvo Ocean Race is around a Clean Seas campaign which is the elimination of plastics in our oceans and the harm that they do to sea life and we saw an opportunity to bring this here to demonstrate to the delegates who report there
Script: Spokesperson for the V&A Waterfront Donald Kau says they clear 81 tonnes of waste from the water every year
Claire “Can it operate 24 hours a day
Donald “ The battery life on the devise itself will allows it to run for eight hours at any given time but it’s got sensors on board that allow it to avoid collision. So we could really effectively put it into the water and let it run for extended periods of time including night time
Script: It can be operated manually with the remote control, or autonomously plotting a route using google maps. Aeroview also operates remotely, directing farmers to problem trees, via the scouting app.
James “So you can actually mark out which trees you want to investigate in the field and that scouting app like Google Maps app and will guide you to those trees in the field.
Script: Hein can sit in Cape Town and guide a farmer in Limpopo to a problem tree he detects on a his farm. Aeroview can map almost anything including large amounts of trash in the water. So Richard and James, have combined their inventions to tackle the scourge of pollution in the popular recreation area of Zandvlei
Richard ] 09 08 50 02 using aerobotics technology they would be able to fly over Zandvlei and identify biomass in the water ..that would then allow our drone to tap into their GPS and their imaging... and go in an collect the trash and go in and extract what shouldn’t be in the water
Script: Zandvlei is the last functioning estuary in Cape Town, providing a vital nursery for fish stocks in False Bay, but keeping it clean is a massive problem explains Dalton Gibbs of the City of Cape Town
Dalton With the first rain and hoping for the rains obviously in Cape Town the first rains come in autumn will bring a big flush of litter down when those streets get flushed clean .
Script: The canals that feed into Zandvlie are more, like trash conveyor belts
Dalton It's polluting that system which is essentially our food chain at the end of the day but it's a hazard for recreational use aesthetically it's really bad. It clogs the ecosystem and then obviously all the decomposing products all the plastic waste in particular is a negative chemical feedback into system in the long term
Claire Dalton what your first impression of seeing the Wasteshark in action
Dalton “Really interesting definitely holds promise
Script; And both these South African start-up companies are showing promise internationally making in-roads into global markets.
